title: Prioritized wishlist cliffs: compact synthesis + action items (Jul 2026)
summary: Working synthesis of customer asks collected between May–Jul 2026. Compact view focused on high-impact themes, frequency signal, proposed quick wins, and suggested owners for handoff to product and eng. This is a working doc; some items need engineering validation for effort estimates.
notes:
Context: Post-Q2 capture across enterprise trials, Dedicated onboarding calls, and hosted API support tickets. We prioritized asks by frequency (loose count), customer tier (enterprise vs startup), and measurable impact on adoption/cost.

Method: pulled items from recent CS interviews (10), support queue flags, and two customer workshops. Rough counts appended below. Not exhaustive; intended to guide next 2-week tactical work.

Interpretation rules (brief):
- Frequency labels: S (single customer), F (few, 2–4), M (many, 5+).
- Tier weight: E (enterprise), S (startup).
- Impact estimate: qualitatively high/med/low (business impact on adoption or retention).

High-level themes:
1) Cost visibility & per-route breakdown (M, E|high): repeated asks for token-level cost by model + route + timeframe; several customers said current cost dashboards are too coarse to debug spikes.
2) Faster & safer fallbacks (F, E|high): need predictable routing policies when primary model saturates, with preserved prompt structure and deterministic fallback mapping.
3) Private deployment onboarding friction (F, E|med): documentation gaps in network config and KMS flows; a couple of pilots delayed by infra ops approvals.
4) SDK + example parity (M, S|med): multiple engineering teams request complete parity between SDKs (node/python/go) for streaming and function-calls.
5) Quantization & perf guidance per workload (M, S/E|high): customers want explicit recommended model variants and quantization profiles for common workloads: chat w/ long context, embeddings, and reranking.
6) Observability: token-level traces + cold-start attribution (F, E|med): product teams want traces tied to request ids to diagnose tail latency.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Effort for per-route cost breakdown: does current billing pipeline have token attribution? Needs infra check.
- Fallbacks: can runtime preserve tokenization/kv cache across variants? Ask Serving Runtime leads.
- Private docs: can we assemble a validated runbook for partner infra with step-by-step network checks?

Tone: mix of direct customer quotes and paraphrase below; flagged items are ones CS thinks will materially reduce friction or reduce incoming tickets (reduction estimate in parentheses).
top_asks: Per-route, per-model token cost breakdown in console + API (M, E|high)
Deterministic fallback policies with clear compatibility mapping and SLA behavior (F, E|high)
Private deployment quickstart runbook for infra teams (S/F, E|med)
SDK parity: streaming + function-calls in Go SDK with the same helper utilities as Python/Node (M, S|med)
Model/quantization recommendations page with workload templates (M, S/E|high)
Token-level tracing linked to request IDs for tail-latency debugging (F, E|med)
priority_matrix:
Suggested triage:
- P0 (2–4 week delivery): Per-route cost API + console (small UI + backend aggregation), SDK parity critical path for Go streaming (small-medium), Private runbook (doc + scripts).
- P1 (1–3 months): Deterministic fallback implementation (runtime + routing policy work), Model recommendation portal with vetting and examples.
- P2 (3+ months): Deep tracing integration and cost-attribution rework requiring billing pipeline changes.

Rationale: Cost visibility and SDK parity are high-frequency, relatively contained work that unblock multiple customers. Fallbacks are technically trickier but high impact for enterprise SLAs.
sample_customer_quotes: "We had a surprise 3x bill spike last month and couldn't tell which route caused it — the dashboard aggregates everything." — Large fintech trial (E)
"When the primary model throttled, the fallback returned a different response shape and broke our downstream parsing. Need deterministic fallbacks." — SaaS search product (S)
"Our infra team needs a short step-by-step for VPC peering and KMS trust — the generic guide was good but not prescriptive enough." — Healthcare pilot (E)
"Go SDK streaming is still missing the helper that rewrites chunked responses into a single event stream; our backend is Node-first but wants Go parity." — Platform engineering (S)
"We want explicit guidance: for reranking at 512 tokens pick X-quantized and this batch size for cost/perf. Right now it's guessing." — AI-native startup (S)
"Tracing per token woud be overkill, but tying token counts and cache hit info to request IDs would let us see if KV cache is saving latency." — Retail enterprise (E)
